title: AI stocks drag Wall Street lower, S&P 500 slumps 2.6%
summary: AI stocks are pulling Wall Street lower again amid ongoing worries that the sector is in a bubble.

image.caption: People who work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange are seen on Tuesday. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)

blocks.text: AI stocks are pulling Wall Street lower again amid ongoing worries that the sector is in a bubble.
The market is heading back to where it was before Monday's relief rally
The S&P 500 index fell 2.6 per cent on Wednesday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 831 points, or 1.7 per cent. The Nasdaq composite fell 3.8 per cent.

In Toronto, the S&P/TSX Composite index slipped by 1.9 per cent. Technology and mining stocks were the biggest decliners, led by electronics manufacturer Celestica, and several gold and silver companies.
The stock market appears to be heading back to where it was before Monday's relief rally, sparked by the surprise return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Meanwhile, U.S. President Donald Trump plans to move ahead with a new round of wide-ranging tariffs as the latest data shows inflation remains stubbornly high.
Treasury yields fell in the bond market.
